heroHeadline: Sharara Oil Field Shutdown Nears a Week as NOC Weighs Force Majeure, While Libya's Mufti Warns Against a Haftar Power-Sharing Deal
heroSubtitle: An armed group's Sep 21 closure of Valve No. 7 on the Sharara–Zawiya pipeline has cut Libya's largest oil field from ~300-350K bpd to ~100-105K bpd; NOC said Sep 25 the closure has cost roughly 720,000 cumulative barrels and continues to warn — without yet declaring — force majeure, as the Zawiya refinery and Brega Marketing gate blockade from Sep 22 only partially eased. Separately, Grand Mufti Sheikh Al-Sadiq Al-Gharyani renewed a Sep 24 public warning against a reported US-brokered power-sharing deal that would install Saddam Haftar as president alongside Dbeibah as prime minister, calling it a foreign-backed 'major conspiracy'; the same day, Presidential Council head Mohammed Menfi met US adviser Massad Boulos in New York, welcoming unification efforts while stressing 'Libyan ownership of the political process.' No new assassinations or oil-infrastructure drone strikes were confirmed this period.
footerNote: Data sourced from official reports, major outlets, and institutional analyses.
